_about: The ontology's identity: its release rises on every published change, `extends` names what it composes on top of, `carries` what the directory holds.
name: policy
summary: Access policy as facts on the data layer: a rule permits or forbids a permission (an action on a kind of resource, narrowed by a selector) for a role or a team, a table or a column carries its classification and whether it holds personal data, a principal holds roles and an agent is granted some, the active rules compile into a Cedar bundle the deploy pipeline carries, and an agent running for a principal gets the signed intersection of what the two may do. The generated system's IAM is derived from the same rules through the principals its components run as, into the platform's bindings as nodes of its own, shipped with the system and never enforced by OTO.

changelog.note: On its own (ADR-0006, step 4): the pack extends data and agent only. The generated system's bindings are IamBinding nodes of the pack's own (provider, resource_uri, bindings, withheld, generated_by) that bind one resource, grant the principals and derive from the rules; resource_uri on DataStore, Component and Interface moves here from the architecture pack; the calm adapter exports binding nodes as controls when both packs are composed. The compiler, the snapshot, the IAM derivation, the two stages, the command, the write hook and the served read hook live in oto/packs/policy and are loaded through this manifest. PL8 reworked, PL9 added.

The generated system's IAM (roadmap E7, ADR-0005): on the architecture pack too; a Component or a System runs_as a Principal, a Permission carries the platform role it maps to (cloud_role), a Table its resource_uri, safeguards widened to Table and Column, a generated Control derives_from the rules; `oto policy iam` writes build/iam (bindings, the gcp form, the controls proposal, a signed manifest) and applies the controls through the gates. PL8. The sample's invoice intake service runs as its own account and writes the invoices table.

Principal (a person's or a service's identity that holds a session) with holds_role, and granted_role for the agent pack's Agent, so `oto policy snapshot --agent --principal` writes the signed intersection of what the two may do (roadmap E3); on data and agent. PL6, PL7.

First release (roadmap Epic E, E1): PolicyRule and Permission on data, a rule for a role or a team with one permission and optional resources, classification and pii on Table and Column, a table holding personal data when a column does, PL1-PL5, awaiting confirmation. ADR-0004 chooses Cedar as what the rules compile to.
